review_notes: Read the whole target (426 lines), the definition of CKN.IsWeakDivFreeL2 and dotLinear in JSpace.lean, the relevant definitions in FourierRealification.lean (complexifyVectorL2, realPartVectorL2, realLerayProjection, realStokesOperator), the multiplier definitions in FourierLeray.lean (lerayProjectionL2, lerayFourierMultiplier, stokesL2Operator, stokesFourierMultiplier), all in-file uses of fourier_postcompCLM in other Leray files, and the relevant Mathlib files (Analysis/Fourier/FourierTransform.lean, Analysis/Distribution/SchwartzSpace/Fourier.lean, .../Basic.lean, MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/ContinuousLinearMap.lean). The file's statements are mostly already at the natural level (isWeakDivFree_congr_ae, realPartVectorL2Representative_eq_ae, realPart_isWeakDivFree_of_fourierOrthogonal). Two generalizations are supported: the domain of fourier_postcompCLM, and the input type of the two '*Representative_isWeakDivFree' theorems. No compilation was possible, so the proposed signatures are unverified; in particular the general-V form of fourier_postcompCLM still needs the SchwartzMap Fourier instance binders [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V]. I did not treat purely unused binders (e.g. [CompleteSpace G]) as findings on their own, only as a remark inside a finding.

findings.excerpt:
theorem fourier_postcompCLM
    {F G : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F] [CompleteSpace F]
    [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℂ G] [CompleteSpace G]
    (L : F →L[ℂ] G) (f : SchwartzMap L2Vec3 F) :
    𝓕 (f.postcompCLM L) = (𝓕 f).postcompCLM L := by
findings.problem: The statement is the general fact that the Schwartz Fourier transform commutes with postcomposition by a continuous complex-linear map, but its domain is hard-wired to L2Vec3 even though the proof never uses anything specific to L2Vec3. The proof body only rewrites with the generic lemma Real.fourier_eq, moves the scalar through L pointwise, and applies L.integral_comp_comm to f.integrable; all three are available for an arbitrary finite-dimensional real inner product space. Because the lemma is stated on L2Vec3, the file's own Vec3-domain Schwartz object weakTestSourceSchwartz (a SchwartzMap Vec3 ℝ), and any user working in the physical coordinates Vec3 rather than the Hilbert coordinates L2Vec3, cannot use it. The lemma is reused in three other files (FourierJApproximationOrthogonality.lean line 102, ForcedRegularisedFourierGradient.lean lines 153 and 165, ForcedRegMomentumTransport.lean line 113), all of which would keep working after the generalization. (Additionally, [CompleteSpace G] is not used: postcompCLM only needs G to be a normed space over ℝ and ℂ, and ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm requires completeness only of the source F; this is secondary and not the main point.)
findings.proposed_change:
State the lemma over a general finite-dimensional real inner product space:

  theorem fourier_postcompCLM
      {V F G : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]
      [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V]
      [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F] [CompleteSpace F]
      [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℂ G]
      (L : F →L[ℂ] G) (f : SchwartzMap V F) :
      𝓕 (f.postcompCLM L) = (𝓕 f).postcompCLM L

The existing proof script should transfer unchanged (ext ξ; the same `change`; two rewrites with Real.fourier_eq; the same integral_congr_ae and L.integral_comp_comm steps), since Real.fourier_eq, SchwartzMap.integrable and ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm are all stated for arbitrary inner-product-space domains. The only elaboration obligation added is the SchwartzMap Fourier instFourierTransform binder set for V, which is exactly the same binder required by Mathlib's generic Schwartz Fourier lemmas. Current uses with V = L2Vec3 are recovered by inference. I have not compiled this variant.
findings.benefit: The lemma becomes reusable for all Schwartz Fourier computations over an arbitrary Euclidean domain (in particular Vec3, the coordinate space the same file already works with via weakTestSourceSchwartz) instead of only over L2Vec3, without changing any downstream use. It also aligns the lemma with the generality of the surrounding Mathlib API (SchwartzMap.fourier_evalCLM_eq is stated for arbitrary V), so users do not have to re-derive or copy it when they move to physical coordinates.

findings.problem: Both theorems state weak divergence freedom only for the complexified image of a real field, although the proofs never use the special form of the argument. In realLerayProjectionRepresentative_isWeakDivFree the argument complexifyVectorL2 f is used only as an opaque element of ComplexVectorL2: after applying realPart_isWeakDivFree_of_fourierOrthogonal it just unwinds the definition of lerayProjectionL2 (ℱ.symm (lerayFourierMultiplier (ℱ ·))) and invokes lerayFourierMultiplier_divergence_free_ae on ℱ (complexifyVectorL2 f). The same happens in realStokesOperatorRepresentative_isWeakDivFree, whose argument complexifyTensorL2 F is used only as an arbitrary element of the tensor L² space when calling stokesFourierMultiplier_divergence_free_ae. Hence the theorems describe only a proper subrange (the realifications) of the actual multiplier maps, even though lerayProjectionL2 and stokesL2Operator are total maps on all complex L² fields.
findings.proposed_change:
State the representive theorems for an arbitrary complex input, and derive the current real statements as one-line corollaries:

  theorem realLerayProjectionRepresentative_isWeakDivFree (v : ComplexVectorL2) :
      CKN.IsWeakDivFreeL2 (realPartVectorL2Representative (lerayProjectionL2 v)) :=
    realPart_isWeakDivFree_of_fourierOrthogonal v (by
      -- ℱ (lerayProjectionL2 v) = lerayFourierMultiplier (ℱ v), then divergence-free a.e.
      ...)

  theorem realLerayProjectionRepresentative_isWeakDivFree_real (f : RealVectorL2) :
      CKN.IsWeakDivFreeL2
        (realPartVectorL2Representative (lerayProjectionL2 (complexifyVectorL2 f))) :=
    realLerayProjectionRepresentative_isWeakDivFree (complexifyVectorL2 f)

and analogously

  theorem realStokesOperatorRepresentative_isWeakDivFree {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t)
      (G : ComplexTensorL2) :
      CKN.IsWeakDivFreeL2 (realPartVectorL2Representative (stokesL2Operator ht G))

with the existing statement recovered by G := complexifyTensorL2 F. The proofs transfer verbatim because the only facts used about the input are 'ℱ (multiplier (ℱ ·)) = multiplier (ℱ ·)' (ℱ.apply_symm_apply) and the a.e. divergence-free range lemma, neither of which mentions complexifyVectorL2 or complexifyTensorL2. The downstream users are unaffected: realLerayProjection_isWeakDivFree and realStokesOperator_isWeakDivFree, and the consumers in ForcePressureOperator.lean, FourierPhysicalJRange.lean and SmoothingTimeRegularityCore.lean, all go through the real statements, which remain as corollaries. I have not compiled this variant.
findings.benefit: The result then states the actual range property of the Leray projection and Stokes operator on the whole complex L² space (which is what the underlying Plancherel argument proves), rather than only on the realification subspace. Users who obtain a complex velocity/tensor field not defined as a complexification of real data can apply the theorem directly, and the real statements, which are what the applications use, remain available with no extra work.
